questions.q: Why is variation important for a species, and how does sexual reproduction promote it?

answer.text: Variation means differences among the individuals of a species. It is important because environments keep changing, and if a population has variety, some individuals are likely to have features that let them survive a new challenge such as heat, cold or disease. Variation is thus the raw material of evolution and helps a species survive over time.

In sexual reproduction two parents contribute genetic material through gametes. The mixing of DNA from the mother and father, along with the reshuffling of genes when gametes are formed, produces offspring that differ from each other and from their parents.

answer: Because it constantly generates new combinations, sexual reproduction creates far more variation than asexual reproduction, giving the species a better chance of survival.

questions.q: Why is reproductive health important, and what methods are used to prevent unwanted pregnancy and disease?

answer.text: Reproductive health means complete physical, mental and social well-being in all matters relating to reproduction. It is important for spacing children, for the health of the mother and child, and for controlling population and the spread of sexually transmitted diseases.

Several methods are used. Barrier methods such as condoms physically prevent the sperm from meeting the egg. Hormonal methods like oral pills change the hormone balance so that eggs are not released. Devices such as the Copper-T are placed in the uterus, and surgical methods can be used to block the tubes.
Condoms also protect against sexually transmitted diseases like HIV/AIDS.

answer: Awareness of these methods is essential for a healthy society.
